Thick Crust Cottage Cheese Pizza

This thick crust cottage cheese pizza has a soft, chewy crust, plenty of melty cheese, and 17 grams of protein per serving! The easy cottage cheese pizza dough uses simple ingredients and no yeast, so you don’t have to wait for it to rise. Top it with pizza sauce, mozzarella, and turkey pepperoni for an easy, protein-packed pizza night at home.

If you’ve been around here for a while, you know I’m always looking for simple ways to add more protein to everyday meals. Cottage cheese has become one of my favorite ingredients for doing just that. My cottage cheese protein bagels and cottage cheese and egg flatbread are two great examples, and now we’re turning it into a thick, chewy pizza crust!

Blending the cottage cheese with a little olive oil creates a smooth base for the dough, while baking powder gives the crust lift without the need for yeast. The result is a thick, chewy pizza crust that’s sturdy enough to hold plenty of sauce, cheese, and toppings. If you want all the pizza flavor without making a crust, my cottage cheese pizza bowls are another easy, protein-packed option.

The trick to getting that thicker, almost pan-pizza-style texture is keeping the dough to a smaller 9- to 10-inch circle. I also love baking it in a lightly oiled 9-inch metal cake pan. It helps the crust hold its shape while giving the bottom and edges a beautiful golden finish.

And because there’s no yeast or rise time, homemade pizza suddenly feels very doable, even on a busy weeknight.

Pro Tip: Don’t skip the first bake! Par-baking the cottage cheese pizza crust for 10–12 minutes before adding the sauce and toppings helps the center cook through and prevents it from becoming soft or gummy.

Simple Ingredients, Big Pizza Flavor

You only need a handful of everyday ingredients to make the cottage cheese pizza dough, then you can have fun with the toppings. Here’s what you’ll need:

A Few Key Ingredient Notes:

  • Low-fat cottage cheese: The star of the crust! Once blended, cottage cheese becomes completely smooth and adds moisture, tenderness, and extra protein to the dough.
  • Baking powder: Gives the crust its lift and makes this a no-yeast pizza dough, so there’s no rise time required.
  • Pizza sauce: Use your favorite store-bought or homemade pizza sauce. You only need a thin to moderate layer so the thick crust doesn’t become soggy.
  • Mozzarella cheese: Part-skim mozzarella melts beautifully and gives you that classic cheesy pizza topping.
  • Turkey pepperoni: Adds plenty of savory pepperoni flavor while keeping things a bit lighter than traditional pepperoni.

How to Make Cottage Cheese Pizza

Make It Your Own

Turkey pepperoni keeps this version simple and adds plenty of flavor, but this cottage cheese pizza crust works with all your favorite toppings. Try mushrooms, bell peppers, onions, spinach, olives, cooked chicken, or your favorite veggies. Just avoid piling on too many wet toppings, since excess moisture can make the center of a thick crust softer.

Tips for the Best Cottage Cheese Pizza Crust

  • Let it rest before slicing: Those 3–5 minutes really do make a difference. The cheese has time to set and the crust settles slightly, making the pizza easier to slice and giving it a better texture.
  • Blend until completely smooth: Take a few extra seconds to make sure the cottage cheese has no visible curds. This gives you a much smoother, more even dough.
  • Don’t add too much flour: The dough may be slightly sticky when you first bring it together. Add extra flour a little at a time, just enough to make it manageable. Too much can make the crust dry or dense.
  • Keep it small and thick: For that thick, chewy pizza crust, keep the dough around 9–10 inches across. Stretching the same amount of dough into a larger pizza will give you a much thinner crust.
  • Try a cake pan: A lightly oiled 9-inch metal cake pan is my favorite way to bake this pizza. It helps the dough hold its thick shape and encourages the bottom and edges to brown, giving it more of a pan-pizza feel.
  • Use a sturdy metal pan: A light-colored metal pan tends to bake the crust more evenly. Dark pans can brown the bottom and edges more quickly, so keep an eye on the pizza as it bakes.
  • Par-bake before topping: This is especially important with a thicker crust. Giving the dough a head start before adding the sauce and cheese helps prevent a doughy center.
  • Go easy on the sauce: More isn’t always better here! A moderate layer gives you plenty of pizza flavor without weighing down the crust or adding too much moisture.

Thanks so much for reading! If you make this recipe, I would love it if you could give it a ★ rating below. Follow me on YouTube, Instagram, and Facebook for more healthy food inspiration. Cheers!

Thick Crust Cottage Cheese Pizza

This thick crust cottage cheese pizza has a soft, chewy crust, plenty of melty cheese, and 17 grams of protein per serving! The easy cottage cheese pizza dough uses simple ingredients and no yeast, so you don’t have to wait for it to rise. Top it with pizza sauce, mozzarella, and turkey pepperoni for an easy, protein-packed pizza night at home.
Course: Main
Cuisine: American, Italian
Author: Dani Spies
Prep Time20 minutes mins
Cook Time25 minutes mins
Total Time45 minutes mins
Servings: 4 servings
Calories: 259kcal

Save this recipe?

Enter your name and email, and I’ll send it to your inbox. Plus, you’ll get delicious new recipes every week.

Save Post

Ingredients

  • 1 cup low-fat cottage cheese
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 cup all‑purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
  • 1½ teaspoons baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
  • 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder

Toppings

  • 1/3 cup pizza sauce
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 3/4 cup shredded part‑skim mozzarella cheese
  • 10 slices turkey pepperoni
  • optional: parmesan cheese, red pepper flakes, garlic powder

Instructions

  • Place a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 450°F. Lightly oil a 9-inch metal cake pan. You can also use a pizza pan or baking sheet.
  • Blend the cottage cheese and olive oil until completely smooth.
  • In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Add the cottage cheese and combine until a shaggy dough forms. It may be a bit sticky and crumbly, so use your hands to bring it together.
  • Transfer the dough out onto a lightly floured counter and gently knead it a few times, adding a little extra flour as needed, until it comes together into a ball.
  • Press or lightly roll the dough into a round roughly 9–10 inches across, about 1/3–1/2 inch thick.
  • Transfer the dough to the prepared cake pan, pizza pan or baking sheet and press it out to maintain that 9–10‑inch size, pushing it slightly up at the edges to form a higher rim like a pan‑pizza crust.
  • Bake the bare crust for 10–12 minutes, until it looks set and dry on top and lightly golden at the edges but still pale overall, then remove from the oven.
  • Once the crust has done its first bake, pull it out and spread a moderate layer of the seasoned sauce over the warm par‑baked crust, leaving a small border around the edges. Sprinkle with oregano.
  • Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella evenly over the sauce, and then arrange the turkey pepperoni slices over the cheese.
  • Return the pan to the oven and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the crust edges are golden brown. For extra browning, broil for 1–2 minutes at the end, watching closely.
  • Let the pizza rest 3–5 minutes on the pan so the cheese sets slightly and the crust relaxes, then sprinkle with grated Parmesan (if using), and red pepper flakes, slice, and serve.

Notes

  1. Keeping the dough in a smaller 9–10‑inch circle with the full 1:1 batch gives you a noticeably thicker, chewier crust.
  2. A lightly oiled 9-inch cake pan gives you the thickest results as it helps maintain the crust structure. It also helps the bottom brown and gives you that pan‑pizza edge. However, you can still get excellent results on a pizza pan or baking sheet.
  3. Light‑colored, sturdy metal tends to bake more evenly. 
  4. Par‑baking the crust before topping prevents a doughy or gummy center under the sauce and cheese.
  5. Don’t skip the rest after baking. 3–5 minutes lets the structure relax and makes for cleaner slices and better texture.
